title: What actually makes you feel loved at 3am
dek: Not the answer you would put on a dating profile. Twelve questions about the care that lands when the day has fallen over.

questions.prompt: You've had a bad day and someone's already home when you walk in.

options.label: Ask them to sit with you. No talking
Tell them the whole thing, in order
They've made tea and dealt with the thing you were dreading
Go to your room. They let you

questions.prompt: You're at a wedding where you know nobody and the seating chart has betrayed you.

options.label: Find one person and stay with them all night
Text the group chat a running commentary
Learn the DJ's name and become useful
Step outside, call it early

questions.prompt: One thing you'd always have, whatever the budget:

options.label: The thing they mentioned once, in June
A whole weekend with nothing booked

questions.prompt: I'd rather hear it than be shown it.
I check whether someone's upset by how they type.
You get to know one thing about a new partner on day one:

options.label: How they treat the waiter
How they talk about their ex
What they do when plans are cancelled
What they give you for no reason

questions.prompt: I'd rather be needed than wanted.
A friend says they're fine. You don't believe them.

options.label: Say 'okay' and stay close
Ask a second time, plainly
Do one small thing, no announcement
Give them a day, then check in

questions.prompt: Put yourself on the map of how you actually receive love.
questions.helper: Across: tell me or show me. Up: give me room or stay close.

questions.prompt: I remember what people mention wanting.
questions.high: There's a note in my phone

questions.prompt: If I have to ask for it, it doesn't count.
The group chat has a plan tonight. You have a book and no intention of moving.

options.label: Go, and be glad you did
Stay. Send a photo of the book
Invite everyone to yours instead
Say yes, cancel at six

results.name: Words of affirmation
results.tagline: Say it, then say it again
results.blurb: You can survive a bad week on one well-chosen sentence. What lands isn't flattery — it's specificity: someone naming exactly what you did and why it mattered. You replay those lines for years, which is why you're also very good at giving them.
strengths: Makes people feel seen in one sentence
Remembers the exact compliment that helped
Says the thing instead of assuming it's known
results.watchOut: Words are cheap to some people. Let a kind act count even when nobody narrates it.

results.name: Quality time
results.tagline: Presence, with the phone in another room
results.blurb: You don't need a big gesture, you need someone's full attention for an unremarkable hour. Half-listening is worse than absence to you. The people who get this about you are the ones who've seen you relax completely.
strengths: Gives attention that actually feels like attention
results.watchOut: Time is finite. Being present with everyone can mean being absent for yourself.

results.name: Physical touch
results.tagline: A hand on the shoulder fixes more than a speech
results.blurb: You regulate through contact: a hug held a second too long, a shoulder against yours on a sofa. You're not clingy, you're wired this way, and you read other people's comfort with touch unusually carefully because you know how badly it can land.
strengths: Comforts without needing the right words
Warm in a way people remember
results.watchOut: Not everyone wants to be reached for. Ask, even when it feels obvious.

results.name: Thoughtful gifts
results.tagline: Proof you were listening in June
results.blurb: Your love language is evidence: the book they mentioned once, the exact snack, the thing that says I noticed you. It's not about money — a €2 object can wreck you if it's the right one. You keep a mental shelf of everyone's small wants.
results.watchOut: A gift can't replace the conversation. Sometimes the present is just your time.

results.name: Acts of service
results.tagline: Let me take one thing off your list
results.blurb: You show up with the practical thing: the lift, the meal, the form filled in correctly. You'd rather remove a problem than discuss it, and you quietly resent being thanked for what felt obvious. Your care is load-bearing and mostly invisible.
results.watchOut: Not everything needs fixing. Sit with someone before you reach for the toolbox.

results.name: Room to disappear
results.tagline: Close, but with the door shut sometimes
results.blurb: You need solitude the way other people need company, and being checked on can feel like being watched. Your closeness is built on trust, not constant contact: the people you love can go quiet for a week and nothing changes.
strengths: Shows up fully when you do show up
results.watchOut: Silence reads as rejection to people who aren't built like you. Say when you'll be back.
